source.note: Scan without a text layer. National Senior Certificate paper (cover: NATIONAL SENIOR CERTIFICATE; running header: NSC). The PDF includes the cover (printed page 1), the instructions (page 2) and the information sheet (page 10); PDF page n = printed page n. The cover states that the question paper consists of 9 pages and 1 information sheet. Duration 3 hours as printed on the cover. Source file and hash are recorded in sources/maths/manifest.json.

extraction.method: manual transcription from 170 dpi page renders, checked at 400 dpi where needed

questions.text_md: $4x^{2}+3x-5=0$  (correct to TWO decimal places)
$\left(\sqrt{\sqrt{32}+x}\right)\left(\sqrt{\sqrt{32}-x}\right)=x$
questions.notes: Checked at 400 dpi: each radical is a nested square root, $\sqrt{\sqrt{32}\pm x}$, with no additional exponent on the first group.

questions.text_md:
Solve simultaneously for $x$ and $y$:
$y+x=12$  and  $xy=14-3x$

Consider the product $1\times 2\times 3\times 4\times\ldots\times 30$.
Determine the largest value of $k$ such that $3^{k}$ is a factor of this product.
questions.notes: Highest power of 3 dividing $30!$. No dedicated prime-in-factorial skill; tagged with exp.laws-of-exponents.

questions.text_md: Write down the values of the next TWO terms of the sequence.
Determine the general term of the sequence in the form $T_{n}=an^{2}+bn+c$.
Which term(s) of the sequence will have a value of $74$?
Which term in the sequence has the least value?
Determine the value of $K$ if the series has $21$ terms.
Determine the largest value of $n$ for which $T_{n}>\dfrac{5}{8192}$
Without using a calculator, determine the value of:  $\displaystyle\sum_{y=3}^{10}\dfrac{1}{y-2}-\sum_{y=3}^{10}\dfrac{1}{y-1}$

A steel pavilion at a sports ground comprises of a series of $12$ steps, of which the first $3$ are shown in the diagram below.

Each step is $5$ m wide. Each step has a rise of $\dfrac{1}{3}$ m and has a tread of $\dfrac{2}{3}$ m, as shown in the diagram below.

The open side (shaded on sketch) on each side of the pavilion must be covered with metal sheeting. Calculate the area (in m$^{2}$) of metal sheeting needed to cover both open sides.
questions.notes: The printed wording is 'comprises of'. Area of both stepped side elevations of a 12-step pavilion (arithmetic series of rectangular strips). Tagged with seq.arithmetic-series-sum.

questions.stem_md:
Below are the graphs of $f(x)=x^{2}+bx-3$ and $g(x)=\dfrac{a}{x+p}$.

* $f$ has a turning point at C and passes through the $x$-axis at $(1\,;\,0)$.
* D is the $y$-intercept of both $f$ and $g$. The graphs $f$ and $g$ also intersect each other at E and J.
* The vertical asymptote of $g$ passes through the $x$-intercept of $f$.

questions.text_md: Write down the value of $p$.
Show that $a=3$ and $b=2$.
Calculate the coordinates of C.
Write down the range of $f$.
Determine the equation of the line through C that makes an angle of $45^{\circ}$ with the positive $x$-axis. Write your answer in the form $y=\ldots$
Is the straight line, determined in QUESTION 4.5, a tangent to $f$? Explain your answer.
The function $h(x)=f(m-x)+q$ has only one $x$-intercept at $x=0$. Determine the values of $m$ and $q$.

questions.stem_md: Sketched below is the graph of $f(x)=k^{x}$ ; $k>0$. The point $(4\,;\,16)$ lies on $f$.

questions.text_md: Determine the value of $k$.
Graph $g$ is obtained by reflecting graph $f$ about the line $y=x$. Determine the equation of $g$ in the form $y=\ldots$
Sketch the graph $g$. Indicate on your graph the coordinates of two points on $g$.
questions.notes: Sketch of the inverse (logarithmic) graph. No dedicated log-graph-sketch skill; tagged with fn.inverse-exp-log and fn.sketch-exponential.

questions.stem_md: Use your graph to determine the value(s) of $x$ for which:

questions.text_md: $f(x)\times g(x)>0$
$g(x)\leq -1$
If $h(x)=f(-x)$, calculate the value of $x$ for which $f(x)-h(x)=\dfrac{15}{4}$

Two friends, Kuda and Thabo, each want to invest R$5\,000$ for four years. Kuda invests his money in an account that pays simple interest at $8,3\%$ per annum. At the end of four years, he will receive a bonus of exactly $4\%$ of the accumulated amount. Thabo invests his money in an account that pays interest at $8,1\%$ p.a., compounded monthly.

Whose investment will yield a better return at the end of four years? Justify your answer with appropriate calculations.
questions.notes: Kuda uses simple interest $A=P(1+in)$ plus a 4% bonus of the accumulated amount. No dedicated simple-interest skill; tagged with fin.compound-growth.

questions.stem_md: Nine years ago, a bank granted Mandy a home loan of R$525\,000$. This loan was to be repaid over $20$ years at an interest rate of $10\%$ p.a., compounded monthly. Mandy's monthly repayments commenced exactly one month after the loan was granted.

questions.text_md: Mandy decided to make monthly repayments of R$6\,000$ instead of the required R$5\,066,36$. How many payments will she make to settle the loan?

After making monthly repayments of R$6\,000$ for nine years, Mandy required money to fund her daughter's university fees. She approached the bank for another loan. Instead, the bank advised Mandy that the extra amount repaid every month could be regarded as an investment and that she could withdraw this full amount to fund her daughter's studies. Calculate the maximum amount that Mandy may withdraw from the loan account.
Determine $f'(x)$ from first principles if it is given that $f(x)=4-7x$.
Determine $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ if $y=4x^{8}+\sqrt{x^{3}}$
questions.notes: Checked at 400 dpi: the radical is $\sqrt{x^{3}}$ (square root of $x^{3}$), not a cube root and not $(\sqrt{x})^{3}$ written separately.

questions.text_md: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$
$\dfrac{dy}{da}$
questions.notes: Differentiate with respect to the parameter $a$, treating $x$ as constant. No dedicated partial-derivative skill; tagged with calc.power-rule.

questions.text_md: The curve with equation $y=x+\dfrac{12}{x}$ passes through the point $\mathrm{A}(2\,;\,b)$. Determine the equation of the line perpendicular to the tangent to the curve at A.

questions.stem_md: After flying a short distance, an insect came to rest on a wall. Thereafter the insect started crawling on the wall. The path that the insect crawled can be described by $h(t)=(t-6)(-2t^{2}+3t-6)$, where $h$ is the height (in cm) above the floor and $t$ is the time (in minutes) since the insect started crawling.

questions.text_md: At what height above the floor did the insect start to crawl?
How many times did the insect reach the floor?
Determine the maximum height that the insect reached above the floor.
Solve $f(x)=f'(x)$

questions.stem_md: The graphs $f$, $f'$ and $f''$ all pass through the point $(0\,;\,0)$.

questions.text_md: For which of the graphs will $(0\,;\,0)$ be a stationary point?
Explain the difference, if any, in the stationary points referred to in QUESTION 9.2.1.
Determine the vertical distance between the graphs of $f'$ and $f''$ at $x=1$.
For which value(s) of $x$ is $f(x)-f'(x)<0$?
questions.notes: Leads to a cubic inequality after subtracting $f'$. No dedicated cubic-inequality skill; tagged with alg.zero-product and fn.interval-notation.

questions.stem_md: The school library is open from Monday to Thursday. Anna and Ben both studied in the school library one day this week. If the chance of studying any day in the week is equally likely, calculate the probability that Anna and Ben studied on:

questions.text_md: The same day
Consecutive days

questions.stem_md: Events A and B are independent. $\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{A})=0,4$ and $\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{B})=0,25$.

questions.text_md: Represent the given information on a Venn diagram. Indicate on the Venn diagram the probabilities associated with each region.
Determine $\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{A}$ or NOT $\mathrm{B})$.

Motors Incorporated manufacture cars with $5$ different body styles, $4$ different interior colours and $6$ different exterior colours, as indicated in the table below.

The interior colour of the car must NOT be the same as the exterior colour.

Motors Incorporated wants to display one of each possible variation of its car in their showroom. The showroom has a floor space of $500$ m$^{2}$ and each car requires a floor space of $5$ m$^{2}$.

Is this display possible? Justify your answer with the necessary calculations.
